title: The Frontier Perimeter Security Standard
subtitle: A building code for the organizations that build, test, rate, warn about and oversee frontier AI. It asks one question of each: is the edge of this organization sound enough to be trusted near an unreleased model? We inspect to this code from the public record; we do not certify anyone.

tiers.floor: The Floor. The minimum. The least any organization should clear before it is trusted with pre-release model access, or before it asks the world to fix its own weaknesses. Every observable Floor control costs close to nothing to meet. Binary: clears the observable Floor, or has items to resolve.
tiers.std: Standard Practice. Built to spec, not just to code. What an organization that handles unreleased models, or publicly warns about their risk, should demonstrate above the Floor.

levels.1: Curb inspection. Observable from the public record with no cooperation and nothing sent to the organization's systems beyond an ordinary visit to its public website. What this map publishes.
levels.2: Interior inspection. Requires the organization to open the door. Offered to any actor on the map as a self-assessment.

grading: Every control is pass / below-code / recommended / not-observable against a named requirement. No composite score. A permit records that the work met code at inspection; it does not certify the firm will not be breached.

families.name: Email trust
families.q: Can a message forged in this organization’s name reach a lab, a colleague, or the public?

controls.name: Enforcing DMARC
controls.std: Publishes a DMARC policy of quarantine or reject, so receivers act on mail forged in the organization's exact name.

controls.name: SPF hard-fail
controls.std: Publishes an SPF record ending in -all, so unauthorised senders are rejected.

controls.name: DKIM signing
controls.std: Signs outbound mail with DKIM so recipients can verify integrity and origin.

controls.name: Transport hardening (MTA-STS / TLS-RPT)
controls.std: Publishes MTA-STS and TLS reporting so mail cannot be silently downgraded.

controls.name: No live look-alike domains
controls.std: No mail-capable typo or homoglyph look-alike of the organization's domain is registered to a third party.

controls.name: Inbound phishing controls
controls.std: Runs an email security gateway with anti-phishing and impersonation protection.

controls.name: Security awareness training
controls.std: Trains staff against phishing and social engineering on a recurring basis.

controls.name: Strong TLS
controls.std: HTTPS/TLS configuration rates A- or better. Not read in this edition: an independent TLS grade requires a third-party active handshake scan, which this map does not run.

controls.name: HSTS on the public website
controls.std: Serves a Strict-Transport-Security header with a max-age of at least six months on the organization's public website, so browsers refuse a downgrade to plain HTTP.
controls.src: HTTP read of the public homepage

controls.name: Shielded origin
controls.std: Web origin sits behind a CDN or WAF rather than answering directly from an exposed server.

controls.name: No known-exploited vulnerabilities
controls.std: The organization's directly-reachable services carry no known-exploited (CISA KEV) or critical unpatched CVEs.

families.name: Attack surface
families.q: What is the organization leaving open?

controls.name: No exposed admin/database services
controls.std: No RDP, SMB, database, or remote-admin ports reachable on public addresses.

controls.name: DNS & domain hygiene
controls.std: DNSSEC and CAA present; no dangling subdomains vulnerable to takeover.

controls.name: Clean network reputation
controls.std: Addresses do not appear on malware, botnet, or spam blocklists.

families.name: Access & credentials
families.q: How hard is it to get in?

controls.name: MFA everywhere
controls.std: Multi-factor authentication on email, remote access, and all privileged accounts.

controls.name: Privileged access management
controls.std: Administrative access is least-privilege, inventoried, and separated from daily-use accounts.

controls.name: No exposed credentials
controls.std: No corporate credentials for the organization's domain sit in known breach or infostealer dumps.

controls.name: Prompt offboarding
controls.std: Access is revoked promptly when staff or contractors leave.

controls.name: Centralized identity (SSO)
controls.std: Single sign-on with central control over accounts and enforcement.

families.name: Pre-release access
families.q: When a lab hands this organization an unreleased model, what stands between that access and an attacker?

controls.name: Isolated, phishing-resistant pre-release access
controls.std: Pre-release model access (API keys, weights, sandboxes) is held in dedicated accounts protected by phishing-resistant MFA, separate from staff's everyday email and collaboration accounts, and every use is logged.

controls.name: Access ends with the engagement
controls.std: Pre-release credentials and artifacts are revoked or destroyed when the engagement ends, and the organization can show the lab that it happened.

controls.name: No pre-release material in general-purpose tools
controls.std: Pre-release outputs, transcripts and evaluation results are not stored in personal drives, shared chat workspaces or third-party AI tools outside the lab's agreed environment.

controls.name: Named owner for lab relationships
controls.std: A named person is accountable for each lab's access and is the first call if the lab needs to revoke it in a hurry.

families.name: Resilience
families.q: If hit, can the organization recover without paying?

controls.name: Tested, isolated backups
controls.std: Backups are immutable or offline, and restoration is tested.

controls.name: Endpoint detection & response
controls.std: EDR/managed detection across endpoints and servers.

controls.name: Incident-response plan
controls.std: A documented, exercised incident-response plan with defined roles and notification paths.

families.name: Governance & record
families.q: Is the organization a clean, accountable counterparty that can be reached about a flaw?

controls.name: No US Treasury sanctions designation
controls.std: Not designated on any US Treasury (OFAC) list carried in the US Consolidated Screening List: SDN, SSI, NS-MBS, CMIC, CAPTA or PLC. Listings on Commerce (Entity List, Denied Persons, Unverified, Military End User) or State (ISN, ITAR debarred) lists are export-control records: they are shown on the actor's profile as a matter of record and do not count against the Floor.
controls.src: US Consolidated Screening List (trade.gov), exact name and alias match

controls.name: Clean regulatory standing
controls.std: No unresolved enforcement action of concern on the public record. Not read in this edition beyond the screening lists above.

controls.name: Breach transparency
controls.std: Any past breach is on the public regulatory record; the organization can speak to it.

controls.name: Independent security attestation
controls.std: Holds a current SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, or equivalent.

controls.name: Named security contact
controls.std: Publishes a valid, unexpired security.txt (RFC 9116) at /.well-known/, naming where to report a vulnerability. An organization that asks others to fix their weaknesses should be reachable when someone finds one of its own.

controls.name: Carries cyber insurance
controls.std: Holds a current cyber-insurance policy, having passed an underwriter's control bar.

families.name: Data handling
families.q: How is sensitive material held, and who else touches it?

controls.name: Encryption at rest
controls.std: Family data is encrypted at rest, with managed keys.

controls.name: Data residency disclosed
controls.std: The organization can state where its clients' and partners' data physically resides.

controls.name: Sub-processor disclosure
controls.std: Discloses the third parties that touch its clients' and partners' data.

controls.name: AI / LLM data-handling policy
controls.std: Has a stated policy governing whether and how sensitive and pre-release material is exposed to third-party AI tools.

controls.name: Retention & secure deletion
controls.std: Retains sensitive data no longer than needed and deletes it securely.

families.name: Supply chain & continuity
families.q: Does the organization manage the risk behind it, and watch its own systems?

controls.name: Own vendor-risk program
controls.std: Runs its own third-party / sub-processor risk assessment.

controls.name: Independent penetration testing
controls.std: Commissions regular independent penetration tests and remediates findings.

controls.name: Logging & monitoring
controls.std: Centralised logging and monitoring capable of detecting intrusion.

controls.name: Staff background checks
controls.std: Vets staff and contractors who will handle pre-release models, weights or evaluation results.

families.name: Contract
families.q: What has the organization agreed to in writing?

controls.name: Breach-notification SLA
controls.std: The contract commits the organization to notify the counterparty within a defined time of a breach.

controls.name: Right to audit
controls.std: The contract preserves its clients' and partners' right to audit or re-assess the organization's controls.

families.name: Documented exposure
families.q: What does the public record already say has happened?

controls.name: No active leak-site listing
controls.std: Not listed on a ransomware or extortion leak site within the twelve months before the scan. Older listings are shown as a matter of record and do not count against the Floor. A listing is an attacker's claim, not a confirmed breach.

editions: Edition changes from v0.2 (the family-office code): A7 out-of-band payment verification and G2 litigation and offshore context removed as family-office-specific; F1 pinned to named lists; B2 built as an HSTS check; F5 built as a security.txt check and held at Standard Practice until the fetch path is proven on successive scans; family K (pre-release access) added at Level 2.
